cf.title: BUG #19702: decode() accepts Base64 payload after terminal padding

input.subject: BUG #19702: decode() accepts Base64 payload after terminal padding

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The bug report in message #1 states the problem with a reproducible case, and the fix reuses the rule base32hex already applies. The plan in message #3 keeps the stricter rule out of released stable branches, which limits who is affected. Confidence is medium because the code and the callers of pg_b64_decode() were not read.

brief.title: Reject data after padding in base64 decoding
brief.problem: decode(..., 'base64') keeps reading after the terminal "=" padding and adds later characters to the result, so 'YQ==AAAA' returns \x6100 with no error. Applications that use decode() to validate base64 input accept malformed input. pg_b64_decode() in src/common and dearmor() in pgcrypto share the same logic.
brief.proposed_design: The decoders raise an error for anything except whitespace after the padding, the rule base32hex already uses. The fix covers decode() in encode.c, pg_b64_decode() in src/common and the armor decoder in pgcrypto, with regression tests. Daniel Gustafsson squashed the three patches and plans master only, plus the relevant parts for v19.
user_visible_surface: decode(text, 'base64') now errors on characters other than whitespace after terminal padding.
base64url decoding (new in v19) follows the same rule, per the v19 backpatch plan.
pgcrypto dearmor() rejects armor with data after base64 padding, even when the CRC matches.
pg_b64_decode() in src/common rejects the same input, which affects its callers.
author_claims: The decoder sets its end marker at the first "=" and never checks it again, so later data and later "=" pass.
The new rule matches what base32hex already does.
The change rejects input that used to pass, so back branches are left to the committer.
dearmor() shows the same bug when the CRC matches.
brief.thread_state: Daniel Gustafsson reviewed, squashed the patches and will commit to master only; Masahiko Sawada agreed and asked for v19 too, since base64url is new there. Gustafsson agreed to prepare a v19 backpatch of the relevant portions.
unclear: The material does not say which internal callers of pg_b64_decode() exist, such as SCRAM, and whether stricter input could break them.
The thread does not say which portions go into v19 beyond base64url.
The error SQLSTATE and message text for the new rejection are not shown.
There is no release note or documentation change for the stricter behaviour.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: A SCRAM secret in pg_authid with data after the salt padding could stop parsing after pg_upgrade; Postgres does not generate such secrets.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: pg_b64_decode() in src/common/base64.c rejects input it used to accept, which changes behaviour for its callers.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Expression indexes, check constraints or generated columns that call decode(..., 'base64') on malformed rows would fail on restore into the new version.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The patch narrows what decode(), dearmor() and pg_b64_decode() accept, and pg_b64_decode() may serve SCRAM authentication.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The change rejects input that used to pass; the thread plans master only, plus the relevant parts for v19.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a check to the base64 decode loop in encode.c, used for bytea decoding.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which callers of pg_b64_decode() exist, such as SCRAM, and can any of them receive data after padding from a client or stored secret that works today?
Which parts of the squashed patch go into v19 besides base64url decoding?
Which SQLSTATE and message text does the new error use, and do they match the existing base32hex error?
Will the release notes list the stricter decode() and dearmor() behaviour as an incompatibility, including the restore failure for expression indexes and check constraints over malformed rows?

committability.owner_note: Daniel Gustafsson reviewed the pgcrypto part against RFC 9580, squashed the patches and said in message #3 that he will apply them to master.
committability.liability: The owner signs for any report of input that used to decode and now fails, in decode(), dearmor() and callers of pg_b64_decode(), from the first release that carries the change.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted the three patches on the day of the bug report; no sign either way about later fixes.

priority.reason: The three patches are under 8 KiB in total, touch three decoders plus tests, and add no new user-visible surface. A committer who reviewed the code is ready to apply it, and the open points are release-note and v19 scope details.

provisional_note: Without the code I could not check the SQLSTATE and message text, the whitespace handling after padding, or whether SCRAM and other pg_b64_decode() callers can receive data after padding. The cost of the added check in the decode loop was not measured in the thread.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert refactoring of hex code to src/common/
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert refactoring of hex code to src/common/
Reverted commit(s): move hex_decode() to /common so it can be called from frontend; Rework refactoring of hex and encoding routines; Remove PG_SHA*_DIGEST_STRING_LENGTH from sha2.h
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This is a combined revert of the following commits:
- c3826f8, a refactoring piece that moved the hex decoding code to
src/common/.  This code was cleaned up by aef8948, as it originally
included no overflow checks in the same way as the base64 routines in
src/common/ used by SCRAM, making it unsafe for its purpose.
- aef8948, a more advanced refactoring of the hex encoding/decoding code
to src/common/ that added sanity checks on the result buffer for hex
decoding and encoding.  As reported by Hans Buschmann, those overflow
checks are expensive, and it is possible to see a performance drop in
the decoding/encoding of bytea or LOs the longer they are.  Simple SQLs
working on large bytea values show a clear difference in perf profile.
- ccf4e27, a cleanup made possible by aef8948.

The reverts of all those commits bring back the performance of hex
decoding and encoding back to what it was in ~13.  Fow now and
post-beta3, this is the simplest option.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical decoding on standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: Logical decoding on standby

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical Decoding with timelines
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical decoding in the walsender follow timeline changes, as physical replication does, so that logical replication can cascade from a standby. It moved the walsender's send-pointer and timeline logic into shared functions used by both physical and logical sending.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs, the author, withdrew it as Returned with Feedback and said he had a new approach for the next release. Andres Freund noted that it covers only the walsender, while logical decoding also runs through SQL functions. He also said it does not let decoding start on a standby, which also needs forced hot_standby_feedback and slot cleanup in dbase_redo. Michael Paquier reported that the patch no longer applied, the earlier review comments were unaddressed, and no tests were shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Afaics the patch as is won't allow to start logical decoding on a standby.

precedents_retrieved.title: Missing dependency on oauth_validator test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the `oauth_hook_client` binary as a test dependency in the oauth_validator meson.build file, so the binary is built before the test runs. Without it, `meson test --suite oauth_validator` failed when the build did not enable the OAuth test through `PG_EXTRA_TEST`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only message is the author's proposal, and there are no replies.

precedents_retrieved.title: NOT VALID for Unique Indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: Simon Riggs proposed allowing an existing index to be switched between unique and non-unique via ALTER INDEX SET [NOT] UNIQUE [NOT VALID] and ALTER INDEX VALIDATE UNIQUE, so uniqueness could be added without a long write-excluding scan and validated later in a separate transaction. The WIP patch added a new pg_index column (induniquevalid) and did not yet implement the index validation scan.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No deciding objection was raised; reviewers were positive and asked only design questions. The author said he could not finish the patch for the next commitfest and would complete it later, and a later message noted the patch no longer applied to HEAD and asked for an updated version, with no reply shown. The entry was left incomplete with no updated version posted.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I won't be able to finish this patch in time for this next CF, but
thanks for your interest, I will complete for PG15 later this year.

precedents_retrieved.title: Encoding protection for pgcrypto
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgp_sym_decrypt_text and pgp_pub_decrypt_text check that the decrypted result is valid in the database encoding, and raise an error if it is not. It adds regression tests for this and moves some existing tests that failed under some encodings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Cary Huang reported failing tests and questioned aborting the transaction instead of issuing a warning. The author posted v2 and argued that callers who want no encoding check can use the bytea variants, and no later message follows.

precedents_retrieved.summary: to_date_valid()

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement TODOs for index operator strategy number validation
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds strategy number bounds checks to operator class validation for BRIN, GIN, GiST and SP-GiST, implementing TODOs in that code. BRIN and SP-GiST use RTMaxStrategyNumber as the upper limit, GiST uses a limit computed from the Geo* constants, and GIN keeps its existing limit of 63.
precedents_retrieved.objection: GiST, SP-GiST and BRIN set amstrategies = 0, so strategy numbers are defined by each opclass, and the new checks would make amvalidate() reject valid custom opclasses. RTMaxStrategyNumber is not a general limit for these access methods, and the Geo* constants apply only to the built-in GiST point implementation. The author withdrew the patch for rework.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For example, a custom SP-GiST opclass can use strategy 31 if its support
functions understand it, but this patch would make amvalidate() reject
it.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY: validate option presence rather than option values
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes COPY option checks so that a format-specific option such as FORCE_ARRAY or ESCAPE is rejected when it is present at all, rather than only when its value enables it. It also makes COPY report the format conflict before it parses the option argument.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Masahiko Sawada argued that "allowed only when" can be read as "allowed to be enabled only when", and that the patch makes COPY less flexible for tools that generate COPY commands with explicit true/false values. He added that VACUUM treats its boolean options the same way. The author withdrew the patch after Fujii-san raised the same objection on a related patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My concern is that the proposed patch could make the command
unnecessarily less flexible.

precedents_retrieved.title: logical decoding and replication of sequences, take 2
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend logical decoding with a sequence callback, and extend built-in logical replication so publications can include sequences, so that a logical replica's sequences track the primary and do not produce duplicate values after failover. Sequence increments were decoded non-transactionally by default, and transactionally when the sequence's relfilenode was created or altered in an in-progress transaction.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the 2024 'take 2' entry was withdrawn. They do show that an earlier committed version was reverted in April 2022. Review had found that non-transactional sequence changes could be discarded or hit an assertion before the decoding snapshot was consistent, and mixing transactional and non-transactional decoding caused snapshot, abort and streaming problems. The author judged that a fix would need an extensive redesign that was too late for that release cycle, and posted an alternative that WAL-logs sequence state at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The approach combining transactional and non-transactional behavior implemented by the patch clearly has issues, and it seems foolish to hope we'll find a simple fix.

precedents_retrieved.title: Minimal logical decoding on standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows logical decoding on a hot standby. It adds a catalog-table flag to existing WAL records so the standby can detect snapshot conflicts with logical slots, and it drops conflicting slots, including when wal_level on the primary drops below logical.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the entry was withdrawn. The last messages show the patch set needing repeated rebases and its TAP tests failing intermittently: Rahila Syed reported 018_standby_logical_decoding_xmins.pl failures, and Alvaro Herrera found 019_standby_logical_decoding_conflicts.pl timing out after a rebase in March 2020. No later reply from the author is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
Reverted commit(s): Reject concurrent sequence refreshes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f38afa4abb04e85530c94b88daf11c089375daca.

That commit fixed a race that could leave stale sequence values on the
subscriber after 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. It did so by
raising an ERROR during 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'
whenever a sequence synchronization worker was already running for the
subscription.

That approach caused intermittent buildfarm failures, because the existing
tests did not ensure the sequencesync worker had stopped before executing
'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. While discussing how to fix
the tests, we concluded that blocking the command while a sequencesync
worker is running is inconvenient for users. So we will fix the original
race differently in a follow-up commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add missing padding from MemoryChunk struct"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add missing padding from MemoryChunk struct"
Reverted commit(s): Add missing padding from MemoryChunk struct; Use MAXALIGN() in calculations using sizeof(SlabBlock)
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit df0f4feef.  It turns out the problem which was causing
the 32-bit ARM and PPC animals to fail was due to a MAXALIGN problem in
slab.c.  This was fixed by d5ee4db0e.  The padding that was added in
df0f4feef would only do anything on machines where uint64 was not aligned
to 8 bytes.  The 32-bit machines which were failing are not in that
category, so revert this commit.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P1] reverted hex-code overflow checks because they slowed bytea decoding, and [P7] added encoding checks to pgcrypto decryption. Neither concerns trailing data after base64 padding. Message #4 cites an earlier base64url truncation fix backpatched to v19 as a model, not as a rejected attempt.

No standards or compatibility objection holds up. The patch makes decode(..., 'base64') follow RFC 4648, uses the base32hex rule already in the tree, and goes to master only, so no stable branch changes behaviour; v19 is still in RC and base64url is new there. The one break is input such as 'YQ==Yg==', which used to decode and will now fail; that needs a release-note incompatibility entry, a routine step at release time. Without the code, I could not check the SQLSTATE and message text, or whether SCRAM and other pg_b64_decode() callers can receive data after padding from clients that worked before.

The fix changes only how base64 input is checked when it is parsed, so it touches no WAL, page format, catalog, wire message or exported struct. Two edge cases are worth a release-note line but are not objections. Expression indexes, check constraints or stored generated columns that call decode(..., 'base64') on malformed rows would fail when pg_dump output is restored into the new version. A SCRAM secret in pg_authid with junk after the salt padding could stop parsing after pg_upgrade, but Postgres never generates such secrets.

From the security angle the change only rejects malformed base64 that used to pass, which narrows what decode(), pgcrypto dearmor() and pg_b64_decode() accept; it adds no privilege, exposure or resource path. Without the code I could not check whether SCRAM callers of pg_b64_decode() and the new error text leak nothing beyond what current errors already show.

From the maintenance angle this is a small correctness fix that uses the base32hex rule already in core, adds no GUC, catalog, API or dependency, and adds no measurable cost on common paths. Two committers who know the code reviewed it. A remaining risk is pg_b64_decode() callers such as SCRAM verifiers stored in pg_authid by external tools, but that is a compatibility question for another angle.

No existing Postgres feature or extension gives strict base64 checking in decode(), so nothing makes this fix redundant. The patch extends the existing decoders and copies the existing base32hex rule, so it adds no second mechanism. Neither precedent applies: [P1] is a performance revert of hex refactoring, and [P7] is about pgcrypto encoding checks.

This is a correctness fix for a filed bug report (message #1), not a new feature, so the demand test does not apply. Two committers reviewed it and agreed (messages #3 to #5), and keeping it to master and v19 limits who pays for the stricter rule.
